domain_label: Turlock Independent Food & Dining — Business Models & Unit Economics
purpose: A method for reasoning about how each independent food-and-dining format in Turlock and Stanislaus County is actually run as a business — its menu and equipment, staffing and family-labor model, county-health/ABC/commissary licensing gate, cost structure and labeled benchmark margins, supplier chain, and the operating decisions that make the format viable or doom it — without ever stating a named business's dollar revenue as fact.
assumptions: no observed per-business financials supplied; every dollar band is a labeled industry-benchmark estimate scaled by an observable size signal (seats, sqft, staff, format), tagged estimate-not-actual, never a claim of actual revenue for any named business

the universe is the 40 verified independent food businesses in Turlock catalogued in businesses.json (chains excluded), in a town of ~72,900 with ~8,455 CSU Stanislaus undergraduates and a county ag/food-processing workforce
city, county, state and demographic figures used here (population, income, ancestry shares, permit/license fees) are cited public facts from the deep-dive or labeled derivations, not invented
supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference about the realistic supply universe, not confirmed contracts, unless a cited source states the relationship
cost-structure and margin benchmarks are published industry figures (food/labor/prime/net) applied as planning priors, not audited operator P&Ls
exclusions: chain and franchise food operations (the catalog is independents only)
stating any actual dollar revenue, profit, or owner income for a specifically named Turlock business as fact
demand-and-saturation market sizing as a standalone deliverable beyond what is needed to judge a format's viability (the sizing detail lives in the market/reconciled analyses)
non-food retail, grocery-only, and packaged-goods manufacturing except where a food format straddles into a market arm
tax, legal, and immigration advice for an individual operator; this models formats and decisions, not a specific filing

competency_questions.question: What anchors food demand in Turlock and which heritage communities make ethnic formats viable that a generic 73k town would not carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_DEMAND_BASE names the resident/student/ag-workforce demand sources with cited figures and HERITAGE_ANCHORS ties the Assyrian (~20k), Portuguese/Azorean (~7.3%), Mexican (46.1% Hispanic) and Asian (5.6%) shares to the specific formats each sustains

competency_questions.question: Why does Turlock sustain roughly 40 independents and not far more, and how does Modesto cap that ceiling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MODESTO_CEILING explains the 20-minute regional-anchor leakage and SATURATION_WHITESPACE gives the per-format saturation read and where the count is at ceiling versus has headroom

competency_questions.question: How are per-format revenue and margin bands estimated honestly when no per-business revenue is public?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_REVENUE_METHOD states the published-benchmark-times-observable-size-signal method, the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence level and a confirmation path, and COST_STRUCTURE_BENCHMARKS supplies the food/labor/prime/net backbone it scales

competency_questions.question: What licensing must a fixed food facility, a bar-forward concept, and a mobile vendor each clear before opening?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HEALTH_PERMIT, ABC_LICENSE and COMMISSARY_GATE each state the concrete county/city/state requirement and fee with its public source, and identify which is the binding entry gate for that format

competency_questions.question: How does owner/family labor let thin-margin formats survive, and where does that lever break?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAMILY_LABOR_LEVER explains how unpaid/underpaid family labor suppresses the 36-40% labor benchmark and names the formats most dependent on it and the succession/burnout limits

competency_questions.question: What is the real Central Valley input-cost advantage and which suppliers form the realistic supply universe per format?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INPUT_COST_ADVANTAGE quantifies the dairy/produce/egg/meat edge and SUPPLY_CHAIN_MAP names the broadline, tortilla/masa, Mediterranean, seafood and local-carniceria nodes that serve each format, flagged as representative inference

competency_questions.question: What does it take to run a taqueria or taco truck, and why is the commissary the binding gate for the truck?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TAQUERIA_TRUCK_MODEL describes counter/truck operations, marinated-meat cost center, family labor, the benchmark band, and ties the truck's viability to COMMISSARY_GATE

competency_questions.question: Why is the mariscos format the highest food-cost and most fragile model in the set, and how does it still endure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARISCOS_MODEL states the 35%+ food cost, cold-chain/spoilage and shrimp-price exposure, the Lent peak, and why cultural durability offsets margin fragility

competency_questions.question: Why is specialty/drive-thru coffee the best risk-adjusted entry, and what is the cafe unit economics that makes it work?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAFE_COFFEE_MODEL gives the espresso-capital anchor, COGS/labor/rent split, house-roast margin lever, student-calendar demand, and the county-permit-only entry that ranks it the top white space in SATURATION_WHITESPACE

competency_questions.question: What distinguishes the labor-heavy panaderia and specialty-bakery models, and where is their thin margin?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PANADERIA_MODEL and BAKERY_SPECIALTY_MODEL each name the hand-shaping/overnight-shift labor cost, the low ingredient COGS, the multi-profile straddles (bakery+deli+cafe), and the cultural peaks that drive volume

competency_questions.question: How do alcohol-forward gastropub/wine-bar and capital-intensive fine-dining models differ in their margin engine and entry barrier?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GASTROPUB_MODEL identifies alcohol as the margin engine gated by the Type 47 secondary-market wall, and FINEDINING_MODEL pairs its high gross with the thin 3-8% net and the Modesto destination-dining cap

competency_questions.question: How do the Assyrian/Mediterranean and Italian/pizzeria formats convert heritage demand and the Valley dairy edge into a viable model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASSYRIAN_MED_MODEL ties the kebab-grill equipment, halal supply and ~20k-community anchor (and the market-arm diversification) to viability, and PIZZERIA_ITALIAN_MODEL names the mozzarella-price risk offset by the dairy advantage

competency_questions.question: Why is the ice-cream/dessert model the most weather-sensitive, and how does idle-winter fixed cost shape its viability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ICECREAM_MODEL explains the ~5-6 warm-month revenue concentration, the in-house batch-freezer capex versus scoop-only, and the dairy advantage, with the idle-winter fixed-cost caveat

competency_questions.question: Given demand, cost, licensing and saturation, what is the merged go/no-go on adding a given format in Turlock?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_GO_NOGO composes saturation, cost gate and demand headroom into a defensible add/avoid verdict (no sixth taqueria, fourth mariscos, fourth fine-dining; favor specialty coffee, Asian/Assyrian fast-casual, Portuguese sit-down) each conditioned on clearing the permit and Type 47 gate

glossary.definition: The binding honesty label on every dollar band in this KB: the figure is a published industry benchmark (revenue per seat/sqft/employee or per shop) scaled by an observable Turlock size signal, never a reported or claimed actual revenue for any named business.
Food cost plus labor cost as a share of revenue; the central operating-health metric for a restaurant, targeted at 55-65% across these formats, above which net margin collapses.

The use of owner and family members as unpaid or below-market labor, which structurally suppresses the published 36-40% full-service labor benchmark and is the main reason thin-margin Turlock ethnic independents survive.

A permitted commercial kitchen or permanent food facility that a mobile vendor must operate in conjunction with for overnight parking, water/waste servicing and prep; under Stanislaus County rules it is mandatory and is the binding cost gate for the truck format.

California ABC on-sale general license (full liquor with food) whose secondary-market value can exceed $100k-$200k in a tight county, making it the real entry wall for any bar-forward Turlock concept, distinct from the cheaper Type 41 beer-and-wine license.

The demand cap created by Modesto (roughly triple Turlock's population, 20 minutes north) siphoning destination, fine-dining and national-concept spend, the main force keeping the independent count near 40 and capping a fourth fine-dining room.

A local ancestry community large enough to sustain a format a generic town would not carry: Turlock's ~20k Assyrian population, ~7.3% Portuguese/Azorean share, 46.1% Hispanic (mostly Mexican-origin) base, and 5.6% Asian share.
An observable proxy (seat count, square footage, staff count, daily covers, format) used to scale a published per-unit benchmark into a planning revenue band, in place of unavailable actual sales.

The unbroken refrigeration required for raw-seafood mariscos service, the highest food-safety class in the set, whose failure means spoilage loss and health-code exposure, driving the format's 35%+ food cost and fragility.

A full-line foodservice wholesaler (e.g., Sysco Central California in Modesto, US Foods, membership Restaurant Depot) supplying meat, produce, frozen, dry goods, paper and smallwares to most Turlock formats.

nodes.definition: Establish the demand floor every Turlock food format draws on: ~72,900 residents at a median household income of ~$82,995, ~8,455 CSU Stanislaus undergraduates whose term-time presence disproportionately lifts coffee, fast-casual and value demand, and a large county ag and food-processing workforce that drives early-morning, cash-friendly demand. The BLS 2024 food-away-from-home spend (~$3,945/household) across ~25,000 occupied households yields a labeled-estimate resident pool of ~$99M/yr (range $90M-$115M, medium confidence). This is the size of the pie before any format question is asked.

included: resident population, income and household count
CSU Stanislaus student demand
ag/food-processing workforce demand
labeled food-away pool estimate

pros.claim: Sizing the pool from cited public figures grounds every format judgment in real local demand instead of national job-board noise
pros.example: the ~$99M food-away pool from 25,000 households times the BLS $3,945 average sets a defensible ceiling no single format can exceed

cons.claim: A pool average invites the error of dividing it by 40 and calling the result a typical business
cons.example: naively reading ~$99M as ~$2.5M per outlet ignores chain capture and the long full-service right tail

failure_modes: treating the resident pool as the independents' addressable revenue without subtracting chain capture
ignoring the term-time swing of student demand and over-building for a 12-month calendar
acceptance_tests: the demand base cites population, household count, student enrollment and the food-away pool with its range and confidence, all labeled estimate where derived
revisit_triggers: a Census ACS refresh changes population or income
CSU Stanislaus enrollment shifts materially
the BLS food-away spend figure is updated

base.update_signal: a population, income, enrollment, or food-away spend figure is updated

nodes.definition: Tie Turlock's unusual heritage depth to the specific formats it sustains. The town holds California's largest Assyrian community (~20,000, ~a quarter of town; south Turlock historically nicknamed 'Little Urmia'), a ~7.3% Portuguese/Azorean ancestry kept alive by ongoing Azores immigration, a 46.1% Hispanic base that is overwhelmingly Mexican-origin, and a 5.6% Asian/South-Asian share. Each community anchors formats a generic 73k town would never carry — kebab/Assyrian houses and Assyrian markets, Azorean bakeries, panaderias and mariscos, taquerias — which is precisely why Turlock over-indexes on ethnic independents per capita.

included: Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean, Mexican, Asian ancestry shares with sources
the format each community anchors
the per-capita ethnic over-indexing it explains
excluded: the cost structure of each format

pros.claim: Mapping ancestry shares to formats explains both why a format exists and how durable its demand is
pros.example: the ~20k Assyrian community makes three kebab/Mediterranean houses well-matched rather than over-built

cons.claim: Heritage demand is culturally durable but not necessarily growing, so it can be mistaken for a growth lane
cons.example: treating a saturated mariscos count as expandable because the Mexican base is large, ignoring price sensitivity

failure_modes: assuming a large community implies unlimited format headroom
overlooking that the most price-sensitive community caps check averages even where demand is deep
acceptance_tests: each of the four heritage communities is given its cited share and the specific format(s) it anchors, distinguishing durable from growing demand
revisit_triggers: ancestry shares shift in a Census refresh
a heritage community grows or contracts via migration
a new format tied to an under-served community opens

base.update_signal: a heritage community's size or the format it anchors changes

nodes.definition: Account for the single biggest cap on Turlock food demand: Modesto, roughly triple the population and 20 minutes north, is the regional dining anchor. Destination dining, national concepts and big-box variety leak there, which is the main force keeping Turlock's independent count near 40 and capping a fourth fine-dining room. Any format judgment that ignores this leakage will over-state Turlock headroom — especially for cross-shopped, discretionary formats (fine dining, gastropubs) as opposed to neighborhood-loyal ethnic ones.

included: Modesto's size and proximity
which spend categories leak to it
which formats are most vs least exposed to leakage
excluded: the measured leakage figure (it is an estimate of behavior, not a count)

pros.claim: Naming the leakage explains why population alone over-predicts Turlock's restaurant count
pros.example: discretionary fine-dining demand leaks to Modesto, so Turlock's three fine-dining rooms sit at ceiling not headroom

cons.claim: The leakage is an estimate of cross-shopping behavior, not a measured figure, so it can be over- or under-applied
cons.example: assuming all discretionary spend leaks when downtown Turlock retains a loyal date-night base

failure_modes: applying the ceiling uniformly to neighborhood-loyal ethnic formats that do not cross-shop
treating the leakage as measured when it is a behavioral estimate
acceptance_tests: the analysis states Modesto's size and distance and ranks formats by exposure to leakage, flagging the figure as a behavioral estimate
revisit_triggers: a major dining development opens in Modesto or Turlock
a cross-shop leakage study is produced
Turlock downtown dining density changes

base.update_signal: regional dining supply in Modesto or Turlock shifts

nodes.definition: Lay down the published, cited cost-structure backbone every format model is read against: food cost QSR 28-32% / casual 30-34% / fine dining 32-35%; labor QSR 30-32% / full-service 36-40% (median FSR ~36.5%, profitable operators ~34%); prime cost (food+labor) targeted 55-65%; net margin full-service 3-8%, fast-casual 4-10%, QSR 5-12%, coffee 2.5-7% typical (12-15% tightly run). Only ~42% of US restaurants were profitable in 2024. These are planning benchmarks, not audited operator P&Ls, and they are the lens that turns a revenue band into a margin reality.

included: food/labor/prime/net benchmark ranges by service type
the profitability base rate
the planning-prior status of the figures

pros.claim: Pairing every revenue band with the prime-cost and net benchmark stops high gross from being mistaken for high profit
pros.example: a fine-dining room benchmarking $1M+ gross still nets only 3-8%, which the backbone makes explicit

cons.claim: Published benchmarks lag and average away the family-labor and local-input advantages that move real Turlock margins
cons.example: the 36-40% labor benchmark overstates cost for an owner-operated taqueria using unpaid family labor

failure_modes: importing a national benchmark without adjusting for family labor or Valley input costs
reading a benchmark range as a single point estimate
acceptance_tests: food, labor, prime and net benchmark ranges are stated by service type with sources and labeled as planning priors, paired with the profitability base rate
revisit_triggers: a new industry benchmark guide is published
minimum wage or input-cost inflation shifts the labor or food share
a profitability base-rate update lands

base.update_signal: a published cost-structure benchmark or profitability rate is revised

nodes.definition: Define the only honest way to attach a revenue band to a format when no per-business revenue is public: take a published industry benchmark (revenue per seat ~$27 / per sqft ~$150 full-service; coffee median ~$500k at $300-$800/sqft; small bakery $200k-$450k; food truck avg ~$346k) and scale it by an observable Turlock size signal (seat count, sqft, staff, daily covers, format), then tag the result 'estimate, not actual', assign a confidence level, and name the confirmation path (CDTFA / Turlock Finance restaurants-and-hotels sales-tax receipts, or POS seat-times-turn-times-check). The ~$0.9M-$1.25M pool average is a mean pulled up by a full-service right tail, not a typical business; the typical independent clusters $300k-$700k.

included: benchmark-times-size-signal method
the estimate-not-actual label, confidence and confirmation path
the pool-mean-vs-typical-business distinction
excluded: stating a named business's actual revenue

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark band gives a defensible planning number without ever claiming a private business's actual revenue
pros.example: a 40-seat sit-down at ~$27/seat/day scales to a band tagged estimate with a sales-tax confirmation path

cons.claim: A benchmark band can be over-trusted if the size signal is mis-observed or the confidence label is dropped
cons.example: treating a seat-count estimate as precise when the room's turns are unknown

failure_modes: dropping the estimate-not-actual label and presenting a band as a fact
dividing a pool total by outlet count and reporting it as a typical business
acceptance_tests: every revenue band produced carries the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence level, the size signal used, and a named confirmation source, and the pool mean is distinguished from the typical business
revisit_triggers: a published per-seat/per-sqft/per-shop benchmark is updated
CDTFA or Turlock Finance sales-tax data becomes available
a format's observable size signal changes

base.update_signal: a benchmark, a size signal, or the availability of confirming sales-tax data changes

nodes.definition: Explain the swing variable that lets Turlock's thin-margin independents survive: owner and family labor, paid below market or not at all, structurally suppresses the published 36-40% full-service labor benchmark and is the single biggest reason ethnic, owner-operated formats clear a profit on 3-8% net. The formats most dependent on it are panaderias (overnight panadero shift), taquerias and trucks, sit-down Mexican, and mariscos. The lever has hard limits: it caps growth at the family's capacity, masks the true cost of labor when planning a sale, and breaks at succession or burnout.

included: how family labor suppresses the labor benchmark
which formats most depend on it
the succession/burnout/scaling limits

pros.claim: Naming family labor as the survival lever explains how formats run on margins that would sink a fully-staffed operator
pros.example: a panaderia absorbing the overnight panadero shift in-family turns a labor-heavy format profitable

cons.claim: Family labor is invisible on a benchmark P&L, so it understates the true cost to run or buy the business
cons.example: a buyer who must hire out the owner's unpaid hours finds the modeled margin evaporates

failure_modes: modeling a format at benchmark labor cost and missing that its real survival is unpaid family hours
assuming the lever scales when it is capped by one family's capacity
acceptance_tests: the analysis states how family labor moves the labor share, names the most dependent formats, and flags the succession/burnout/scaling limit
revisit_triggers: an operator approaches succession or sale
family capacity changes (illness, departure, growth past it)
minimum-wage changes alter the hired-labor alternative

base.update_signal: a family-labor dependency, succession event, or wage-floor change occurs

nodes.definition: Quantify the genuine Central Valley input-cost and freshness edge that underpins many Turlock formats: the town sits in California's top dairy county group and a major produce/almond/poultry belt, giving short freight, direct-from-grower and carniceria options, and a dense Mexican/Assyrian/Portuguese grocery ecosystem that doubles as specialty-input supply. The edge is real for cafes and creameries (local dairy), pizzerias (cheese), panaderias and Portuguese bakeries (eggs/dairy), and ethnic operators (local carnicerias and halal markets) — a measurable cost and freshness advantage over coastal metros, though it does not offset volatile commodity swings (mozzarella, shrimp).

included: the dairy/produce/egg/meat local edge
which formats benefit most
the limits of the edge against commodity volatility

pros.claim: The local input edge is a real margin cushion that helps explain how thin-margin formats clear a profit
pros.example: a creamery sourcing local cream lowers its dominant COGS line below a coastal competitor's

cons.claim: The edge is on staples, not on volatile or specialty inputs, so it can be over-credited
cons.example: the dairy advantage softens but does not erase a mozzarella price spike for a pizzeria

failure_modes: crediting the local edge for inputs it does not cover (imported specialty, seafood)
assuming freshness alone offsets a commodity price swing
acceptance_tests: the edge is stated for dairy/produce/eggs/meat, mapped to the formats that benefit, and bounded against volatile commodity inputs
revisit_triggers: a major commodity price swing (cheese, eggs, shrimp)
a local supplier or grower channel opens or closes
regional ag output shifts

base.update_signal: a local input channel or commodity price materially changes

nodes.definition: Map the realistic supply universe each format draws on, flagged as representative inference rather than confirmed contracts: the broadline spine (Sysco Central California in Modesto ~15 mi, US Foods, membership Restaurant Depot — with the announced Sysco/Jetro-Restaurant Depot 2026 consolidation as a watch item), tortilla/masa (Tortilla Plug, Romero's, Mi Rancho, Masienda, or local tortillerias), Mediterranean/Assyrian importers (Sadaf, Zarrin, Karabetian, Macar, plus local Assyrian grocers), seafood (Pucci, Sierra Gold, Santa Monica, Catalina for Baja species), and local carnicerias/dairies/produce houses. Only La Mo's (local-farm sourcing) and Ishtar (its own market as input) have documented input links.

included: broadline, tortilla/masa, Mediterranean, seafood and local supplier nodes per format
the inference label on supplier-to-business links
the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation watch

pros.claim: A format-to-supplier map shows the realistic, verified-to-serve-this-geography supply universe behind each model
pros.example: mariscos draws on Pucci/Sierra Gold/Catalina for Baja species fitting Sinaloa-style menus

cons.claim: Supplier-to-named-business links are inference and can be mistaken for confirmed contracts
cons.example: asserting a specific taqueria buys from a named tortilla distributor without a cited source

failure_modes: upgrading a representative supplier link to a stated fact
ignoring the consolidation watch that could move small-operator cash-and-carry pricing
acceptance_tests: each major format has its key supplier nodes named with the supplier-link inference label, and the only documented links (La Mo's, Ishtar) are distinguished from inferred ones
revisit_triggers: the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation completes or changes pricing
a named distributor enters or exits the Valley
a documented supplier contract surfaces

base.update_signal: a supplier relationship, consolidation, or documented link changes

nodes.definition: Establish the baseline licensing every fixed food facility must clear: a Stanislaus County food-facility health permit (plan check plus annual permit) is required for every fixed food facility, and the City of Turlock business license is $114. This is the non-negotiable floor under every sit-down, counter, cafe and bakery model — cheaper and faster than the ABC or commissary gates but mandatory, and the plan-check step is where kitchen layout, equipment and food-safety class are reviewed before opening.

included: county food-facility health permit and plan check
$114 city business license
the mandatory-floor status for fixed facilities

pros.claim: Treating the county health permit as the mandatory floor prevents a model that ignores the plan-check gate
pros.example: a sit-down concept budgeting for plan check and the $114 license before lease signing

cons.claim: The health-permit floor is modest, so it can lull an operator into underestimating the costlier ABC and commissary gates
cons.example: assuming a low health-permit cost means easy entry for a bar-forward concept

failure_modes: skipping plan check and discovering a non-conforming kitchen after build-out
confusing the cheap fixed-facility permit with the costlier mobile or alcohol gates
acceptance_tests: the county health permit (plan check + annual) and the $114 city license are stated with their public sources as the mandatory fixed-facility floor
revisit_triggers: county or city fee schedules change
a food-safety class reclassification alters plan-check requirements
a facility changes its menu/equipment enough to require re-permitting

base.update_signal: a county health-permit or city license requirement or fee changes

nodes.definition: Define the alcohol-licensing gate that governs every bar-forward concept. ABC Type 41 (beer & wine, eating place) costs ~$905 to apply with a $400-$900 population-based annual fee — accessible, and the route for wine bars and food-forward rooms (Vito's, Camp 4). ABC Type 47 (full liquor with food) costs $6,275-$16,560 to apply with a $925-$1,450 annual, but the binding barrier is the secondary-market license value, which can exceed $100k-$200k in a tight county — the real entry wall for tap houses and taverns (10 East, Gray's). Alcohol is the margin engine for these formats, so the license cost is what gates whether the engine can be installed.

included: Type 41 vs Type 47 application and annual fees
the Type 47 secondary-market wall
which formats need which license

pros.claim: Distinguishing Type 41 from the Type 47 secondary-market wall shows the true entry cost of a bar-forward concept
pros.example: a beer-and-wine creperie clears Type 41 cheaply while a full-liquor tavern faces a six-figure Type 47 license

cons.claim: The secondary-market Type 47 value is county- and timing-dependent, so the six-figure figure is a range not a quote
cons.example: a license freeing up at a lower price in a softer market than the cited ceiling

failure_modes: budgeting only the ABC application fee and missing the secondary-market license purchase
choosing a full-liquor concept when a Type 41 beer-and-wine model would clear demand at a fraction of the cost
acceptance_tests: Type 41 and Type 47 fees are stated with sources, the secondary-market wall is flagged as the binding barrier, and the right license is matched to the bar-forward formats
revisit_triggers: ABC fee schedules change
the county license cap or secondary-market price moves
a format shifts between beer-wine and full-liquor

base.update_signal: an ABC fee or secondary-market license value changes

nodes.definition: Establish the binding cost gate for the mobile (truck/cart) format. A Stanislaus County mobile food-facility permit runs $69-$548/yr across four risk categories, the City of Turlock mobile facility permit is $900 (requiring a site plan, county health permit, and commissary + restroom forms), the city business license is $114 — but the structural requirement is the commissary: the county mandates that a mobile vendor operate 'in conjunction with a commissary or other permanent food facility' for overnight parking, water/waste servicing and prep. The recurring commissary fee, not the truck itself, is the real entry and survival gate, which is why 'low-capital truck' is demand-true but cost-gated.

included: county mobile permit $69-$548
city $900 mobile permit + $114 license
the mandatory commissary requirement as the binding gate

pros.claim: Identifying the commissary as the binding gate corrects the 'cheap truck' illusion with the real recurring cost
pros.example: Taqueria Hidalgo's 15-year run proves the truck-plus-commissary model works only when the commissary cost is sustained

cons.claim: Commissary arrangements vary, so the cost gate is a structural fact whose magnitude depends on the specific kitchen deal
cons.example: a truck sharing a commissary with a restaurant at a favorable rate versus paying a standalone fee

failure_modes: budgeting the truck and permits but not the mandatory ongoing commissary
assuming a truck can operate without a permanent-facility tie
acceptance_tests: the county and city mobile permit fees and the mandatory commissary requirement are stated with sources, and the commissary is identified as the binding cost gate
revisit_triggers: county or city mobile-permit fees change
the commissary requirement or a vendor's commissary arrangement changes
a new commissary kitchen opens or closes locally

base.update_signal: a mobile-permit fee or commissary requirement changes

nodes.definition: Map the capital-equipment intensity that gates format entry independent of demand: the espresso machine plus grinders are the cafe's capital anchor; the panaderia and specialty bakery need a baking line (revolving/rack ovens, mixers, sheeters, proofers); mariscos require a heavy cold line for strict cold-chain integrity; the Assyrian/Mediterranean format is defined by its charbroiler/kebab grill; in-house ice cream needs a batch freezer, pasteurizer and hardening freezer (versus a scoop-only shop); pan-Asian needs wok plus tandoor/curry stations. Two concepts can face the same demand but very different up-front capital, so capex is a real go/no-go input beside licensing.

included: the defining capital equipment per format
in-house vs scoop-only and similar capex forks
capex as a demand-independent entry gate

pros.claim: Surfacing capex intensity shows why a demand-true white space may still be hard to enter
pros.example: in-house creamery capex (batch freezer + pasteurizer) gates a format whose demand looks easy

cons.claim: Capex figures vary widely by new-vs-used and scale, so this is a relative-intensity ranking not a quote
cons.example: a used espresso machine and oven dropping cafe entry cost well below a new build-out

failure_modes: judging a white space on demand alone and ignoring its capital anchor
treating capex as fixed when used equipment changes the entry cost materially
acceptance_tests: each major format's defining capital equipment is named and the capex forks (in-house vs scoop-only, etc.) are identified as demand-independent entry gates
revisit_triggers: equipment prices or financing terms change
a used-equipment opportunity changes a format's entry cost
a format adds or drops a capital-intensive station

base.update_signal: equipment cost, financing, or a format's station set changes

nodes.definition: Model the taqueria (sit-down/counter, e.g. La Taqueria, Tacos California, Taqueria La Primera) and taco truck (e.g. Taqueria Hidalgo, cash-only, 15 years at one location). The cost center is marinated meats (asada, al pastor, carnitas, lengua, tripa); tortillas/chips, produce and dried chiles complete the build. It runs QSR/fast-casual economics — food 28-32%, labor 30-32% (lower with family labor) — at value price points and high volume. Counter taquerias benchmark $300k-$720k and trucks $250k-$490k (avg ~$346k), both estimate-not-actual. The sit-down side is at/near saturation; trucks are the low-capital, expandable end, but every truck is cost-gated by the mandatory commissary.

included: taqueria and truck operations and menu
marinated-meat cost center
the benchmark bands and saturation read
the commissary tie for trucks

pros.claim: The model shows why the truck is the cheapest legitimate entry into the sector once the commissary is secured

nodes.definition: Model the Mexican panaderia (e.g. Panaderia Los Compadres, open 7 days with a likely wholesale arm to local taquerias/markets; Panaderia San Miguel, specialty breads and tres leches). The dominant cost is hand-shaping labor on an overnight panadero shift, on top of a capital-intensive baking line (revolving/rack ovens, mixers, sheeters, proofers); ingredient COGS (flour, sugar, lard, eggs, yeast, piloncillo) is low. That gives a low-COGS, labor-heavy, thin-margin profile benchmarking $200k-$450k (estimate-not-actual), with strong Dia de los Muertos and Dia de Reyes peaks. Family labor on the overnight shift is what makes the margin work; there is slight count headroom given the Hispanic share.

included: panaderia menu, baking line and overnight labor
low-COGS labor-heavy margin profile
cultural peaks and the benchmark band

nodes.definition: Model the mariscos (Mexican seafood) format (e.g. Mariscos Culiacan Sinaloa-style raw bar, Mariscos Guayabitos coastal styles, Alegre Marisquero). It runs a heavy cold line under strict cold-chain integrity — raw seafood is the highest food-safety class — and the cost center is fresh shrimp, fish, oysters and octopus, the highest food cost in the entire set (often 35%+) and the most exposed to shrimp/fish price swings and spoilage loss. It benchmarks $500k-$1M (estimate-not-actual, low-med confidence) with a Lent demand spike. The format is count-saturated and margin-fragile but culturally durable: the existing three are defensible, a fourth is not advisable.

included: mariscos cold line and food-safety class
seafood as highest-food-cost center and price/spoilage risk
Lent peak, benchmark band and saturation read

pros.example: a Sinaloa-style raw bar carrying 35%+ food cost and full shrimp-price exposure

nodes.definition: Model the cafe/coffeehouse (e.g. Alison's, Cafe Rome creperie, Grace and Gather, Rise N Brew with a possible house roast, TaZa signature drinks). The espresso machine plus grinders are the capital anchor on a small footprint with high seat-turn at peak; staffing is 3-10/shift, often part-time students. COGS runs 25-35%, labor 30-40%, rent under 12%, net 2.5-7% (12-15% tightly run); a house roast is a real margin lever (green coffee $4-7/lb vs $8-14/lb wholesale roasted). It benchmarks $350k-$650k (median ~$500k, estimate-not-actual). Demand tracks the CSU academic calendar; specialty/drive-thru coffee is the clearest growth lane and best risk-adjusted entry, needing only the county permit.

COGS/labor/rent/net split and house-roast lever
student-calendar demand and the specialty/drive-thru growth lane

CSU enrollment or commuter patterns shift
a new specialty/drive-thru concept enters

nodes.definition: Model the bakery-cafe / European & Portuguese specialty bakery cluster (Sunrise Bakery & Cafe; Olde Tyme Pastries running bakery+deli+espresso bar — three margin profiles in one; Mary Ann's bakery + mini-market; and the under-served Azorean bakery white space). Profile: low ingredient COGS, high labor, plus a high-margin beverage line, prime ~55-65%, blended bands $300k-$600k for the bakery-cafe and $150k-$400k for the festa-concentrated Portuguese bakery (estimate-not-actual). The straddles (bakery/deli/cafe/market) diversify revenue and cushion the room; wholesale adds thin-margin volume. The Portuguese/Azorean bakery is the most seasonal in the set (festa-concentrated), a genuine heritage white space against the 7.3% ancestry.

festa seasonality and the Portuguese white space

nodes.definition: Model the Assyrian/Mediterranean format (House of Kabobs traditional Assyrian; Patogh Mediterranean+Assyrian; Ishtar Mediterranean Market & Grill — grill plus Assyrian market). The charbroiler/kebab grill is the defining equipment; the cost center is halal lamb and chicken plus basmati, bulgur, spices, tahini, olives and lavash, sourced through Mediterranean/Assyrian importers (Sadaf, Zarrin, Karabetian, Macar) and local halal markets. As full-service it runs food 30-34%, labor 36-40%, benchmarking $600k-$1.2M (estimate-not-actual). The ~20k Assyrian community makes three rooms well-matched rather than over-built; Ishtar's market arm vertically integrates supply and diversifies revenue, cushioning the restaurant. Assyrian fast-casual/grab-and-go is an identified white space for lunch/student traffic.

the ~20k-community anchor and well-matched count

nodes.definition: Model the Italian/pizzeria cluster (Villa Napoli SF-style sit-down; Vito's authentic pizza + homemade Italian with a Type 41 wine list; Dean's family pizza + Italian sandwiches; Rico's popular pizza). Pizza is the classic high-margin format — low food cost on dough/sauce/cheese when volume is good — but mozzarella/cheese is the major, volatile cost and the main margin risk, partly offset by the Valley dairy advantage (cheese is often a dedicated dairy contract). Sit-down Italian carries flour, cured meats, canned tomatoes, olive oil and wine. The cluster benchmarks $600k-$1.2M for full-service Italian and a high-margin pizza profile (estimate-not-actual) and reads as balanced at four rooms.

sit-down Italian inputs and the dairy offset
Type 41 wine-list straddle and the balanced count

nodes.definition: Model the gastropub/tavern/wine-bar format (10 East Kitchen & Tap House burgers+brews with a likely Type 47 draft system; Gray's Tavern; Camp 4 Wine bar+lunch on a Type 41/02). Alcohol is the margin engine — the high-margin beverage line carries the model over full-service food inputs. The defining barrier is licensing: a tap house or tavern needs a Type 47 whose secondary-market value can exceed $100k-$200k, while a beer-and-wine bar clears the cheaper Type 41. It benchmarks $600k-$1.3M (estimate-not-actual, low-med) and reads as balanced but downtown-dependent. The format is demand-true but cost-gated: the Type 47 wall, not ingredient cost, decides entry for bar-forward concepts.

the Type 47 vs Type 41 entry wall
downtown dependence and the benchmark band

nodes.definition: Model the ice-cream/dessert format (House of Random ice cream + desserts; Oak Barrel Ice & Creamery, family-owned homemade in-house ice cream). It is the most weather-sensitive format in the set: revenue concentrates in ~5-6 warm months while idle-winter fixed cost pressures net margin. In-house production (batch freezer, pasteurizer, hardening freezer) is materially more capital- and skill-intensive than a scoop-only shop but draws on the Valley dairy advantage on its dominant cream/milk cost. High gross margin per scoop, benchmarking $250k-$500k (estimate-not-actual, low confidence given seasonality). Slight count headroom, but any pro forma must model the off-season fixed-cost drag, not just the warm-month gross.

nodes.definition: Model the contemporary American / fine-dining format (Atrium; Bistro 234, chef-driven and voted Most Romantic, a date-night destination; Roth Social House). It carries the highest labor ratio in the set (labor 35-40%, food 32-35%, premium center-of-plate from Sysco/US Foods plus Central Valley local farms/ranches) and benchmarks an expected Turlock case of $0.9M-$1.5M (national top-end to $2M; estimate-not-actual, low-med). The defining caveat is that high gross does NOT mean high net — net is still only 3-8%. It sits at ceiling because the Modesto destination-dining draw caps a fourth room; a Turlock fine-dining concept realistically lands in the lower half of the band given that leakage.

nodes.definition: Synthesize the per-format saturation read that explains why ~40 is the equilibrium and where headroom remains. At/near ceiling (do not add): mariscos (3, margin-fragile), sit-down Mexican (3), sit-down taqueria (3), contemporary American/fine dining (3-4, Modesto-capped). Balanced/selective: Assyrian/Mediterranean (3), Italian/pizzeria (4), gastropub/wine bar (3). Headroom/white space, ranked: specialty/drive-thru coffee (best risk-adjusted, county permit only), South-Asian/Asian fast-casual (vs 5.6% Asian + students), Portuguese/Azorean sit-down or bakery-cafe (vs 7.3% ancestry, festa-seasonal), Assyrian fast-casual/grab-and-go, healthy fast-casual bowls, dessert/late-night. The ceiling is set by the demand floor, heritage depth (raiser), the Modesto cap (capper) and format-level saturation.

the ranked white-space list
the four forces behind ~40
excluded: the cost-gate verdict (that is the go/no-go node)

cons.claim: Saturation reads are medium confidence absent a measured cross-shop leakage study

treating a mature heritage format as a growth lane

revisit_triggers: a cross-shop leakage study lands

base.update_signal: a format count, leakage measurement, or demand-base figure changes

nodes.definition: Compose the merged go/no-go verdict on adding or running a given format, the synthesis the whole KB builds toward. It intersects three lenses: demand headroom (SATURATION_WHITESPACE), the cost/licensing gate (HEALTH_PERMIT, ABC_LICENSE, COMMISSARY_GATE, EQUIPMENT_CAPEX), and the margin reality (COST_STRUCTURE_BENCHMARKS, FAMILY_LABOR_LEVER). The reconciled rule: do not add a sixth taqueria, a fourth mariscos, or a fourth fine-dining room; the defensible headroom is specialty/drive-thru coffee, Asian/South-Asian and Assyrian fast-casual, Portuguese sit-down, and healthy fast-casual — each viable only after clearing the county-permit (and, for bar concepts, Type 47) cost gate. A white space that is demand-true but cost-gated is a no-go until the gate is cleared.

included: the three-lens go/no-go intersection
the named add/avoid verdicts
the cost-gate condition on every white space
excluded: the underlying saturation or licensing detail (those are their own nodes)

pros.claim: The merged verdict prevents the classic error of acting on demand headroom while ignoring the cost gate
pros.example: ruling a low-capital truck a no-go until the mandatory commissary cost is secured

cons.claim: A single verdict can over-simplify a format whose demand, cost and margin point in different directions
cons.example: a Portuguese sit-down with real demand but festa-seasonal cash flow needing nuance beyond go/no-go

failure_modes: issuing a go on demand alone without confirming the cost gate is clearable
treating the verdict as static when a fee, license value or count changes it
acceptance_tests: the verdict for a format states the saturation read, the binding cost gate, the margin reality, and an add/avoid call conditioned on clearing the permit and Type 47 gate
revisit_triggers: a saturation read changes
a licensing fee or Type 47 value moves
a heritage or student demand shift reorders the white space

base.update_signal: a saturation read, cost gate, or demand shift changes a format verdict

the pool sizing is the sector envelope inside which the per-format benchmark bands must sum
the revenue-band method pairs each band with the food/labor/prime/net backbone so gross is read against margin
the family-labor lever is defined as the suppression of the published labor benchmark
the local input edge moves the food-cost line of the benchmark backbone
capex sits beside the operating benchmarks as the up-front cost the margin must later service
the supplier map is the concrete expression of where the local input advantage is realized
alcohol licensing is layered on top of the mandatory fixed-facility health permit
the mobile commissary requirement extends the fixed-facility permitting floor to trucks
the cafe model leans directly on the student-calendar slice of the demand base
family labor is what lets the value-priced taqueria/truck clear its thin per-order margin
the marinated-meat and tortilla supply nodes feed the taqueria/truck cost center
the truck half of the model is only viable once the mandatory commissary cost is secured
the overnight panadero shift is the family-labor lever that makes the labor-heavy panaderia work
the Hispanic base anchors panaderia demand and its cultural peaks
the seafood supplier nodes and cold chain define the mariscos cost center and its fragility
the Mexican base gives mariscos its culturally durable demand despite margin fragility
the espresso-machine capital anchor is the cafe's defining entry cost
the Portuguese/Azorean ancestry defines the festa-seasonal specialty-bakery white space
the halal and Mediterranean importer nodes feed the kebab-house cost center
the ~20k Assyrian community is the anchor that makes three rooms well-matched
the Valley dairy advantage partly offsets the volatile mozzarella cost that drives pizzeria margin
the Type 41 wine-list straddle (e.g. Vito's) sits on the beer-and-wine license tier
the Type 47 secondary-market wall is the binding entry gate for the bar-forward gastropub
the in-house batch-freezer/pasteurizer capex fork defines ice-cream entry cost
the Valley dairy advantage lowers the creamery's dominant cream/milk cost
the highest-labor-ratio and premium-COGS backbone pins the thin-net caveat on fine dining
the Modesto destination cap pins the Turlock fine-dining case to the lower half of the band
the cafe model's growth read feeds the top-ranked white space in the saturation synthesis
the mariscos margin-fragility read feeds the at-ceiling judgment in the synthesis
the saturation read is the demand-headroom lens of the merged go/no-go verdict
the commissary gate is the binding cost condition on any mobile white space verdict

heritage depth pushes the viable format count up while the Modesto draw pulls it down, and a format read can over-weight one
edges.resolution_rule: apply heritage depth to neighborhood-loyal ethnic formats and the Modesto cap to discretionary cross-shopped formats; when both bear on one format, let the more price-sensitive or more cross-shopped force dominate the saturation read

edges.why_related: the bottom-up per-format bands sum well below the top-down pool-average per business, tempting a false reconciliation
edges.resolution_rule: treat the ~$0.9M-$1.25M pool average as a mean pulled up by a full-service right tail, label it low confidence, and use the per-format bands ($300k-$700k typical) as the primary defensible view

edges.why_related: a demand-true white space can still be capital-gated, so capex constrains which headroom is actually enterable

conflict_axes.name: pool_average_vs_typical_business
conflict_axes.description: A top-down pool-average revenue per business (~$0.9M-$1.25M) conflicts with bottom-up per-format bands that cluster far lower ($300k-$700k).
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: label the pool average a mean pulled up by a full-service right tail at low confidence; use the per-format bands as primary

conflict_axes.name: heritage_depth_vs_modesto_cap
conflict_axes.description: Heritage communities raise the viable format count while Modesto's draw caps it; a format read can over-weight either force.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply heritage depth to neighborhood-loyal ethnic formats and the Modesto cap to discretionary cross-shopped ones

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_cost_gate
conflict_axes.description: A format with real demand headroom may still be cost-gated by licensing, commissary or capex, so demand-true is not the same as enterable.
poles: enter only where the cost gate clears
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true but cost-gated white space as a no-go until the binding gate is cleared

conflict_axes.name: high_gross_vs_thin_net
conflict_axes.description: High-revenue formats (fine dining, gastropub, mariscos) can post strong gross while netting only single digits, so revenue must never be read as profit.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the revenue band with its prime-cost and net benchmark before judging attractiveness

conflict_axes.name: family_labor_survival_vs_scalability
conflict_axes.description: Owner/family labor lets a thin-margin format survive but caps growth and breaks at succession, so the survival lever is also a growth ceiling.
poles: lean on family labor to survive
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use family labor to clear thin margins but model hired-labor cost before assuming growth or a sale

conflict_axes.name: cultural_durability_vs_margin_fragility
conflict_axes.description: A culturally vibrant format (mariscos) can be the most financially fragile, so durable demand does not imply a safe margin.
poles: treat cultural demand as a growth lane
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: defend the existing culturally durable count but do not add to a margin-fragile, count-saturated format on demand alone

conflict_axes.name: type47_full_liquor_vs_type41_beer_wine
conflict_axes.description: A full-liquor bar margin requires a six-figure Type 47 license while a cheaper Type 41 limits the beverage program; the engine versus the entry cost trade.
poles: stay within the affordable beer-wine tier
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: choose Type 41 unless the concept's economics genuinely require and can fund the Type 47 secondary-market license

conflict_axes.name: in_house_craft_vs_capex_burden
conflict_axes.description: In-house production (ice cream, house roast, scratch baking) raises quality and margin per unit but adds capital and skill burden a buy-in model avoids.
poles: make in-house for margin and quality
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: go in-house only where the volume and warm-season demand service the added batch-freezer/oven/roaster capex

conflict_axes.name: seasonal_peak_revenue_vs_idle_fixed_cost
conflict_axes.description: Festa, summer and holiday peaks concentrate revenue while off-season fixed cost drags net, so an annual band hides the cash-flow reality.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: model working capital across the season, not on the annual average, for ice cream, Portuguese bakery, panaderia and mariscos

edge_cases.description: A mozzarella price spike erases a pizzeria's structural margin advantage
edge_cases.trigger: a cheese commodity swing outruns the Valley dairy contract
edge_cases.mitigation: lock a dedicated dairy contract and treat the dairy edge as a cushion, not an immunity, to cheese volatility

edge_cases.description: A cold-chain failure causes spoilage loss and a food-safety exposure at a mariscos room
edge_cases.trigger: refrigeration lapse on a raw-seafood line, the highest food-safety class
edge_cases.mitigation: monitor cold-chain integrity continuously and model spoilage loss into the already-thin mariscos margin

edge_cases.description: A truck is budgeted on the vehicle and permits but not the mandatory ongoing commissary
edge_cases.trigger: a low-capital-truck plan omits the recurring commissary fee
edge_cases.mitigation: secure and price a commissary arrangement before the truck launches; the commissary is the binding gate

edge_cases.description: A bar-forward concept is planned without securing the six-figure Type 47 license
edge_cases.trigger: a full-liquor tavern budgets only the ABC application fee
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm Type 47 availability and secondary-market cost, or scope the concept to Type 41 beer-and-wine

edge_cases.description: An ice-cream pro forma reads warm-month gross and ignores idle-winter fixed cost
edge_cases.trigger: an annual band averages away the off-season cash crunch
edge_cases.mitigation: model working capital across the ~5-6 warm months and the idle winter separately

edge_cases.description: A Portuguese/Azorean bakery's festa-concentrated revenue creates a between-festa cash crunch
edge_cases.trigger: the festa season ends and daily counts fall sharply
edge_cases.mitigation: build a festa-season order book and a year-round product line to smooth cash flow

edge_cases.description: The pool-average revenue per business is reported as a typical business figure
edge_cases.trigger: someone divides the ~$35M-$50M pool by 40 outlets
edge_cases.mitigation: label the average a pool mean at low confidence and lead with the $300k-$700k typical per-format bands

edge_cases.description: A named business's revenue is requested or asserted as an actual figure
edge_cases.trigger: a question demands the real sales of a specific Turlock restaurant
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse to state actual revenue; provide only a labeled benchmark estimate with confidence and a sales-tax confirmation path

edge_cases.description: A supplier-to-named-business link is upgraded from inference to a stated contract
edge_cases.trigger: an answer asserts a specific restaurant buys from a named distributor without a source
edge_cases.mitigation: keep supplier links labeled representative inference except the documented La Mo's and Ishtar cases

edge_cases.description: A demand-true white space is treated as enterable while a cost gate blocks it
edge_cases.trigger: a headroom call ignores licensing, commissary or capex
edge_cases.mitigation: run every white space through the cost gate before issuing a go verdict

edge_cases.description: The Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation shifts cash-and-carry pricing small operators rely on
edge_cases.trigger: the announced 2026 acquisition completes and changes Valley wholesale pricing
edge_cases.mitigation: watch the consolidation and diversify supply beyond a single cash-and-carry source

edge_cases.description: A heritage community is treated as a growth lane when it only sustains a stable count
edge_cases.trigger: a large ancestry share is read as unlimited format headroom
edge_cases.mitigation: distinguish culturally durable demand from growing demand before recommending an addition

workflow.action: Size the resident, student and ag demand floor
workflow.description: State the population, household, student and food-away pool figures as cited facts or labeled estimates
workflow.gate: population, household count, enrollment and the food-away pool with range and confidence are stated

workflow.action: Map heritage anchors to the formats they sustain
workflow.description: Tie each ancestry share to its anchored format and durability
workflow.gate: all four communities have cited shares and named anchored formats

workflow.description: Identify which spend leaks to Modesto and which formats are exposed
workflow.gate: Modesto size/distance stated and formats ranked by leakage exposure

workflow.description: State food/labor/prime/net benchmarks by service type with sources
workflow.gate: food, labor, prime and net ranges are stated as cited planning priors

workflow.description: Define benchmark-times-size-signal banding with the estimate label and confirmation path
workflow.gate: every band carries the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence, a size signal and a confirmation source

workflow.action: Identify the family-labor and input-cost levers
workflow.description: Explain how family labor and the Valley input edge move the margin
workflow.gate: the family-labor labor-share suppression and its limits are stated

workflow.description: Name the broadline, tortilla, Mediterranean, seafood and local nodes per format as inference
workflow.gate: each major format has named supplier nodes with the inference label

workflow.action: Establish the licensing and capex gates
workflow.description: State the health-permit floor, the ABC and commissary gates, and capex intensity per format
workflow.gate: the mandatory health permit and the ABC/commissary/capex gates are stated with sources

workflow.description: For each format, state menu, cost center, staffing, benchmark band and saturation tie
workflow.gate: each format names its cost center, labeled band and the gate or lever that decides viability

workflow.action: Model the alcohol-led and capital-intensive formats
workflow.description: Tie gastropub margin to the Type 47 wall and fine dining to the thin-net Modesto cap
workflow.gate: the Type 47 entry gate and the high-gross-thin-net caveat are stated

workflow.action: Synthesize the per-format saturation and white space
workflow.description: Give the at-ceiling/balanced/headroom read and rank the white space
workflow.gate: each format has a saturation read and the white space is ranked

workflow.action: Issue the merged format go/no-go verdict
workflow.description: Intersect demand headroom, cost gate and margin reality into an add/avoid call
workflow.gate: the verdict states the saturation read, binding cost gate and margin reality and is conditioned on clearing the permit and Type 47 gate

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty label dominates any revenue claim
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue is public, so a band may never be presented as an actual figure
dominance_rules.trigger: any dollar figure is attached to a named business or format
dominance_rules.action: tag it estimate-not-actual with a confidence and confirmation path, and refuse an actual-revenue claim

dominance_rules.rule: The cost gate dominates demand headroom in any entry verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: a demand-true white space that cannot clear licensing, commissary or capex is not enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a go recommendation rests on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: withhold the go until the binding cost gate is shown clearable

dominance_rules.rule: Net margin dominates gross revenue in judging attractiveness
dominance_rules.rationale: high-gross formats still net only single digits, so revenue must not be read as profit
dominance_rules.trigger: a format is judged by its revenue band alone
dominance_rules.action: pair the band with its prime-cost and net benchmark before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: The Type 47 wall dominates the bar-forward concept decision
dominance_rules.rationale: the six-figure secondary-market license, not ingredient cost, decides full-liquor entry
dominance_rules.trigger: a full-liquor concept is scoped without confirming the license
dominance_rules.action: confirm Type 47 availability and cost or rescope to Type 41

dominance_rules.rule: The commissary requirement dominates the low-capital-truck illusion
dominance_rules.rationale: the mandatory commissary is the real recurring gate behind the cheap truck
dominance_rules.trigger: a truck is planned without a commissary arrangement
dominance_rules.action: secure and price the commissary before treating the truck as low-cost

dominance_rules.rule: Saturation dominates demand depth for at-ceiling formats
dominance_rules.rationale: a deep heritage base does not justify adding to a count-saturated, margin-fragile format
dominance_rules.trigger: an addition is proposed for mariscos, sit-down Mexican, taqueria or fine dining
dominance_rules.action: default to no-add and defend the existing count

dominance_rules.rule: Per-format bands dominate the pool average for the typical business
dominance_rules.rationale: the pool mean is pulled up by a full-service right tail and is low confidence
dominance_rules.trigger: the per-business average is cited as a typical figure
dominance_rules.action: lead with the $300k-$700k per-format bands and label the average a pool mean

dominance_rules.rule: Documented links dominate inferred supplier links
dominance_rules.rationale: only La Mo's and Ishtar have evidenced input links; the rest are representative inference
dominance_rules.action: label it inference unless it is one of the two documented cases

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the estimate-not-actual label when the band is first produced, not after review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a revenue figure circulating as a fact and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Price the commissary before committing to a truck concept
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a launched truck stalling on an unbudgeted mandatory commissary cost

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm Type 47 availability and cost before scoping a full-liquor concept
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redesigning a bar-forward concept after the six-figure license proves unobtainable

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair every revenue band with its net benchmark in the same step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a high-gross format being approved before the thin net is seen

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run a white space through the cost gate before calling it an opportunity
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a demand-true but cost-gated format and reversing the call

anti_rework_rules.rule: Model seasonal working capital, not the annual band, for seasonal formats
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an ice-cream or Portuguese-bakery plan failing on an off-season cash crunch the annual band hid

anti_rework_rules.rule: Distinguish a pool mean from a typical business before quoting an average
anti_rework_rules.prevents: anchoring stakeholders on a ~$1M average that no typical independent earns

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep supplier-to-business links labeled inference from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an inferred supply link hardening into an asserted contract that must later be corrected

iteration_protocol.trigger: CDTFA or Turlock Finance restaurants-and-hotels sales-tax data becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the labeled revenue bands and pool capture share with confirmed figures and re-rank confidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Census ACS refresh changes population, income or ancestry shares
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the demand floor and re-map the heritage anchors and saturation reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: a commodity price swing (mozzarella, shrimp, cream, eggs) or the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation lands
iteration_protocol.action: update the affected format cost centers and the input-cost and supply-chain nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: an ABC fee schedule or the Type 47 secondary-market value changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the bar-forward entry gate and the gastropub verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: a format opens or closes, changing a per-format count
iteration_protocol.action: update the saturation read and the merged go/no-go for that format

iteration_protocol.trigger: a cross-shop leakage study or measured Modesto-capture figure is produced
iteration_protocol.action: replace the behavioral leakage estimate and re-rank the at-ceiling formats

iteration_protocol.trigger: a county or city permit/commissary fee or requirement changes
iteration_protocol.action: update the licensing-gate nodes and any format whose entry the change affects

priority_rationale: The demand floor, heritage anchors and Modesto ceiling come first because every format judgment depends on knowing the size and shape of demand; the cost-structure backbone, labeled-revenue method, margin levers and supplier map next, because they are the lenses that turn demand into unit economics; the licensing and capex gates next, because they decide enterability independent of demand; the twelve format models then apply all of that to concrete businesses; and the saturation synthesis and merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream output into a defensible add/avoid verdict.
